card.lives_in: Hornchurch, London Borough of Havering, Greater London
card.occupation: Self-employed speech and language therapist, seeing private clients about 12 hours a week (two after-school sessions and a Saturday morning), mostly children with speech sound and language delays
card.education_detail: A-levels in English, Psychology and Biology at a sixth-form college in Romford; BSc in Speech and Language Therapy from City University London (2004); registered with the HCPC. Worked full-time in NHS community paediatric services for about ten years before going private and part-time after her second child
card.household: Lives with her husband Dean (44), who runs his own small electrical contracting business, and their two children, Ruby (11, just started secondary) and Alfie (8). Three-bed semi with a kitchen extension Dean mostly did himself. No pets, though Alfie keeps asking for a dog
card.cultural_background: White British, born at Oldchurch Hospital and grew up in Dagenham before her parents moved out to Elm Park. Her dad was a Ford worker and her mum did school dinners. She was the first in her family to go to university, and she is quietly proud of that and a bit touchy about it. Church of England. Both kids were christened at the local parish church, and she goes at Christmas, Easter and for the school carol service. She thinks of herself as Christian in a values-and-tradition way rather than a weekly-churchgoing way
card.professional_persona: Very organised and good at what she does. She keeps meticulous session notes, colour-coded progress trackers and a waiting list she manages tightly. She is direct with parents, sometimes more than they'd like, and has little patience for families who don't do the home practice. She sets her rates at the top end for the area because she reckons she's worth it, and she isn't shy about pointing out her NHS experience. She gets privately anxious before reports are due and rereads emails several times before sending them
card.sports_persona: Not sporty as such. She does a Saturday parkrun at Harrow Lodge Park when she hasn't got clients, at a steady pace and mainly for headspace, and she tracks every time in an app. She did a couple of terms of reformer Pilates and liked it, but stopped when the price went up. She tolerates watching football because Dean and Alfie are West Ham
card.arts_persona: Reads a lot, mostly literary fiction and the odd bit of popular psychology, and is in a book group with mums from Ruby's old primary school, where she is usually the one who's finished the book and has opinions. She loves a gallery trip into town and will drag the kids to the Tate Modern or the V&A in the holidays whether they want to go or not. She likes musicals, has seen Hamilton twice, and keeps an eye out for West End ticket deals
card.travel_persona: One proper holiday a year, usually a villa in Spain or Portugal with a pool, booked months ahead after a lot of research. She'd love to do more culture-heavy city breaks and talks about Rome and Kyoto. She did Lisbon for her 40th with Dean and still brings it up. She gets anxious about flying and airports and always arrives far too early
card.culinary_persona: Cooks most nights. She plans dinners for the week on Sunday and does a big online shop. She likes trying recipes from Ottolenghi and the Guardian food pages but cooks plainer for the kids. She's quietly snobbish about chains, though she'll go to Nando's for Alfie's sake. Sunday roast most weeks, and a Friday takeaway curry from the local Indian
hobbies_and_interests: interior design Instagram accounts and redoing rooms
skills: scheduling and admin for her small practice
decent at decorating and upcycling furniture
card.career_goals: Wants to build the practice to a point where she can rent a small clinic room rather than working from home and visiting schools. She has thought about taking on an associate therapist and earning off their hours, but worries about the hassle and the risk. She'd like to do some training in selective mutism and possibly some paid CPD teaching. She doesn't want to go back to the NHS
card.voice: Estuary-ish South-East London/Essex accent, but tidied up when she's being professional. She speaks fairly quickly and clearly, using full sentences when she has something to say. She uses 'erm' when she's thinking and 'sort of' a fair bit, and ends sentences with 'you know' or 'yeah?' when she's checking you're with her. She says 'dinner' for the evening meal, 'knackered' after a long week, and 'mum' and 'mate'. She occasionally slips a 'we was' into a story about her childhood, then sometimes corrects herself. She will pick up your phrasing and hand it back to you, sometimes a bit pointedly. She doesn't like silence and will fill it with a clarifying question or a 'sorry, did you mean...?'
card.typing: Proper capitals at the start of sentences, correct apostrophes and full stops. She gets mildly irritated by other people's 'your/you're'. She occasionally uses 'tbh' or 'x' in personal messages, but not in a form. Answers are short but complete, and she sometimes adds a bracketed caveat. No emojis in anything official
card.with_strangers: Friendly enough on the surface and quick to establish she knows what she's talking about. She can come across as a bit guarded or judgemental at first. She asks pointed questions back and doesn't do much small-talk flattery. She warms up if she thinks you're competent, and goes cool and clipped if she thinks you're wasting her time
small_things: Ruby's new school and the amount of homework
what her book group is reading
a new recipe that went down well, or didn't
Dean leaving his work van on the drive at an angle
deeper_things: She feels she gave up a bit of her career and status when she went part-time, and resents it more than she lets on
Her dad's emphysema and her worry about him and her mum
She gets bad health anxiety and Googles symptoms late at night
She sometimes feels she's outgrown some of her old friends from Dagenham and feels guilty about it
She had a difficult second birth with Alfie and a rough patch afterwards that she never got properly seen for
She and Dean argue about money and whether to move further out to Essex
card.webcam_photo: Laptop webcam at a slight upward angle, framing her from mid-chest up, slightly off-centre to the left. Soft daylight from a window off to the right lights one side of her face, and a ceiling spotlight adds a faint shine on her forehead. She has a fair complexion with light freckles and a polite closed-mouth half-smile with a slightly evaluating look. Her shoulder-length highlighted blonde hair has darker roots showing and is tucked behind one ear. She wears tortoiseshell rectangular glasses, small gold hoop earrings and a navy fine-knit jumper. Behind her is a kitchen-diner extension: a grey shaker-style kitchen unit, part of a white quartz worktop with a fruit bowl and a stack of school letters, a wall calendar with coloured writing, and a framed abstract print in mustard and teal. A pendant light hangs at the top of the frame
